ADDED| Abstract
ADDED| Mobile pop-up coffee vendors operate in dynamic physical environments where permanent internet connectivity is absent or prohibitively unstable. TravelBean MNL, a mobile coffee venture based in Tondo, Manila, faces severe operational bottlenecks due to manual paper-based order taking, post-event calculator sales tallying, and unmonitored raw material consumption. Existing commercial point-of-sale (POS) systems either depend strictly on cloud infrastructure or fail to track inventory at the ingredient level (e.g., deducting coffee beans in grams, milk in milliliters, and paper cups in units per beverage sold).
ADDED| VenueVue, engineered by group CTRL+STAY, is an offline-first Point-of-Sale and Inventory Management System engineered specifically to eliminate these operational gaps. Designed around a local client-server model, VenueVue leverages a central host laptop running an offline XAMPP environment (PHP 8.x backend engine and MySQL 8.x relational database) that broadcasts a local Wi-Fi hotspot. To optimize field operations and eliminate cross-platform tablet deployment issues, the client interface is built as a touch-optimized React 19 Single Page Application (SPA) utilizing TanStack Router / TanStack Start, bundled via Vite 8, and styled with Tailwind CSS 4.
ADDED| Tablet devices used by baristas connect locally via standard browsers (or standalone PWA/Kiosk mode) to process orders, calculate totals, and execute automatic recipe-based ingredient deductions without internet connectivity. Simultaneously, a dedicated Mobile Admin Tablet carried by management connects over the same local network to handle real-time inventory adjustments, file imports/exports, and automated compilation of 4-tab Excel reports via PhpSpreadsheet. Post-event data synchronization across devices is supported via local Wi-Fi push, direct USB transfer, or structured Excel/CSV file imports.
ADDED| This project plan details the complete software development lifecycle for VenueVue across a 5-month (20-week) academic timeline running from August 3, 2026, to December 18, 2026. By combining structured SDLC documentation governance with Agile sprint cycles, group CTRL+STAY delivers a zero-subscription software solution that reduces post-event administrative overhead from hours to minutes.
ADDED| Mobile pop-up coffee businesses operating in temporary physical venuesâ€”such as outdoor fairs, private weddings, school events, and corporate pop-upsâ€”face severe operational inefficiencies due to complete reliance on manual paper-based sales tracking and visual inventory estimation. Because event venues frequently lack reliable cellular coverage or public Wi-Fi networks, cloud-based point-of-sale (POS) systems become unusable. Consequently, pop-up vendors suffer from order-taking errors, lost sales logs, stockouts of critical ingredients mid-event, and an inability to analyze event profitability.
ADDED| A quantitative SWOT and problem prioritization analysis conducted by group CTRL+STAY with TravelBean MNL identified seven distinct problems affecting daily operations:
ADDED| | Total absence of an offline POS system
ADDED| | Requires 2 to 3 hours of late-night manual calculation per event; causes operator burnout.
ADDED| | Inefficient product & ingredient inventory tracking
ADDED| | Frequent mid-event stockouts of essential items (e.g., espresso beans, full-cream milk, cold cups).
ADDED| | Visual estimation and post-event manual updates to basic Excel sheets.
ADDED| | Staff remain unaware when raw materials reach critical thresholds, resulting in rejected customer orders.
ADDED| | High labor fatigue reduces overall operational efficiency and business scalability.
ADDED| | A small team (3 members) was forced to divide attention between customer service and manual paperwork.
ADDED| 1.2 Background and Rationale
ADDED| TravelBean MNL operates with three key personnel:
ADDED| Rhona Mae Aganan: Owner & Operations Manager (Order management, administrative reporting, stock monitoring).
ADDED| Jimwell Mamangun: Co-Owner & Logistics Manager (Equipment transport, site setup, stock procurement).
ADDED| Hired Barista: Dedicated staff member (Beverage preparation, espresso extraction, order fulfillment).
ADDED| Pop-up coffee stands assemble finished beverages from multiple raw ingredients. For example, preparing one 16oz Iced Salted Caramel Latte consumes 18 grams of espresso beans, 200 mL of milk, 30 mL of caramel syrup, one plastic cup, one lid, and one straw. Tracking finished items alone leaves management blind to raw material balances. VenueVue solves this by linking sales directly to recipe-mapping relational database tables.
ADDED| 1.3 Objectives
ADDED| | Quantifiable Success Metric
ADDED| | Digitally capture customer transactions at the point of sale.
ADDED| | 100% elimination of paper order slips during event operations.
ADDED| | Immediate sub-second inventory adjustments per ingredient upon transaction completion.
ADDED| | Implement real-time low-stock alerting mechanisms.
ADDED| | System displays visual alert prompts whenever ingredient stock falls below predefined thresholds.
ADDED| | Guarantee complete offline system availability during mobile events.
ADDED| | 100% functional availability with zero internet connectivity required.
ADDED| | Generation of structured 4-tab Excel workbooks (.xlsx) within 10 seconds post-event.
ADDED| | Enable flexible multi-device data synchronization post-event.
ADDED| | Support for 3 distinct data transfer protocols: Local Wi-Fi push, direct USB transfer, and manual Excel import.
ADDED| | Enforce role-based access control (RBAC) across devices.
ADDED| | Strict separation of privileges between Baristas (read/order access) and Owners (full administrative & file control).
ADDED| 1.4 Significance and Scope of the Project
ADDED| The project scope includes user authentication with RBAC, touch-optimized POS ordering, real-time cart and change calculations, recipe-based inventory tracking, low-stock threshold visual alerts, multi-protocol offline data sync, and automated export of 4-tab Excel reports (.xlsx) via PhpSpreadsheet.
ADDED| Physical receipt printing, online cloud infrastructure, hardware barcode scanners, customer loyalty modules, integrated e-wallets, and multi-venue simultaneous sync are excluded to maintain strict offline simplicity and feasibility.
ADDED| 2. Project Organization
ADDED| 2.1 External Interfaces
ADDED| Tablet POS Touch Interface: Responsive React 19 SPA running in browsers or standalone PWA/Kiosk mode on 7-inch to 10-inch mobile tablets.
ADDED| Mobile Admin Console (Admin Tablet): Web management console running on the Operations Manager's tablet for remote inventory edits, stock alerts, and direct file imports/exports.
ADDED| Laptop Administrative Server: Host workstation running XAMPP (Apache, PHP 8.x, MySQL 8.x) kept safely under the counter.
ADDED| Local Wireless Hotspot: Windows Mobile Hotspot broadcasting a local star network within the 192.168.137.x IP range.
ADDED| Excel File Generator: PhpSpreadsheet PHP library generating 4-tab .xlsx workbooks.
ADDED| 2.2 Internal Structure (Three-Tier Architecture)
ADDED| Architecture Tier
ADDED| | Operational Component & Host Device
ADDED| | Core Technical Logic & Protocols
ADDED| Client Tier (Presentation)
ADDED| | Barista Tablets & Admin Tablet (Android / iPad OS)
ADDED| | Client-rendered Single Page Application built with React 19, TanStack Router, Vite 8, and Tailwind CSS 4. Manages UI states, touch inputs, cart logic, and PWA standalone rendering.
ADDED| Communication Layer
ADDED| | Local Wi-Fi Hotspot (192.168.137.x Subnet)
ADDED| | Handles HTTP/JSON requests over local wireless hotspot connection without internet dependencies.
ADDED| Application Tier (Business Logic)
ADDED| | Host Laptop (Local XAMPP Apache Server)
ADDED| | Serves static React 19 build assets and executes back-end business logic in PHP 8.x. Processes orders, executes recipe deductions, manages RBAC, and compiles Excel exports via PhpSpreadsheet.
ADDED| Data Tier (Persistence)
ADDED| | Host Laptop (MySQL 8.x Relational Database)
ADDED| | Preserves master data across 6 relational tables using prepared statements, foreign keys, and audit logs.

ADDED| | Requirements gathering, ERD schema design, system architecture documentation, test strategy creation, and QA oversight.
ADDED| Roquid, Jenny Lyn
ADDED| | QA & Testing Specialist
ADDED| | Test script execution, offline sync validation, PhpSpreadsheet export verification, bug logging, and UAT sign-off.
ADDED| 2.4 Deliverables
ADDED| Software Project Plan & Project Charter Documents (.pdf / .docx)
ADDED| Prioritized SWOT Analysis & Fishbone Diagram Reports (.pdf / .docx)
ADDED| Project Technical Documentation (PTD) & System Architecture Diagrams

ADDED| Figma Interactive Touch UI Wireframes (7 core screens)

ADDED| PhpSpreadsheet Automated 4-Tab Excel Workbook Templates (.xlsx)
ADDED| Comprehensive Test Plan, Execution Logs, and Signed UAT Acceptance Certificate
ADDED| 3. Review of Existing Alternatives
ADDED| System Feature / Criterion
ADDED| | Lavu POS DOCX

ADDED| | VenueVue (CTRL+STAY) DOCX

IndexedDB (doc 2's queue) does *not* require a secure context, so the queue should work — but the "PWA holds the screen offline" claim should be tested on the actual tablets. ## 7. Red flags vs the stated constraints (Flutter + SQLite + PHP/XAMPP + PhpSpreadsheet; Aug 3 → last week of Nov/Dec)

**A. Stack deviations — 2 of 4 constraints are violated in all three documents**
1. **Flutter: absent as a chosen stack in every audited document.** Doc 1 selects `HTML5 / CSS3 / JavaScript ES6+` with `Tailwind CSS v3.x` (no compiled app at all). Docs 2/3 select `React 19` + `TanStack Router/Start` + `Vite 8` + `Tailwind CSS 4`. Doc 3 §4.2 is titled `Rationale for Architectural Stack Pivot (Flutter to React 19 SPA)` and formally argues *against* Flutter. If Flutter is a hard constraint, this is a **scope/architecture violation requiring client-and-adviser sign-off**, and doc 3 is the document that records the decision to abandon it.
2. **SQLite: zero occurrences in the entire extracted corpus** (verified across all 10 files). Every document specifies **MySQL 8.x** under **XAMPP**. If SQLite is the required local store, the plan deviates in all three revisions, and the deviation is *load-bearing*: doc 2's InnoDB `SELECT … FOR UPDATE` row-locking, `ENUM` columns, `LAST_INSERT_ID()`, and `ACID` claims are MySQL-specific and do not port to SQLite unchanged.
3. **Honored:** `PHP 8.x` + `XAMPP` (`v8.2+`) and `PhpSpreadsheet` (`v1.28+`) are consistent in all three documents. PhpSpreadsheet is the *only* stack element stable across the whole set.
4. **The Flutter pivot is retroactively narrated.** Doc 3 claims Flutter APKs "were evaluated during early planning," but doc 1 (the earliest artifact) never mentions Flutter — it went straight to browser HTML/JS. Expect an adviser to challenge this justification.

**B. Offline-first requirement is architecturally weakened**
5. **Tablets are thin clients, not offline-first nodes.** Doc 1 asserts both "real-time… deduction" *and* "devices do not communicate with the laptop during active sales hours." Doc 2 resolves the contradiction by conceding `not complete autonomous operation of each individual tablet` and naming the host as `single authoritative store`. If the deliverable is expected to be offline-first per device (as a Flutter+SQLite design would be), the delivered architecture does not meet that reading — and doc 2's §8 terminology standard exists precisely to retire the earlier `"100% offline on every tablet"` and `"100% fully autonomous tablet"` claims. **If those claims already reached the client, this is a walk-back that needs to be communicated.**
6. **PWA/Kiosk offline behavior needs verification.** Tablets reach the app at `http://192.168.137.x`, which is **not a secure context**, so service-worker-based PWA install/offline caching is not guaranteed over plain-HTTP LAN IPs.
